answerNotes.BALL: A ball is usually round in games such as baseball. American football uses a different, elongated shape.
answerNotes.GAME: Game names the organized activity or contest. Equipment such as a bat or board is used in the game but is not the game itself.
answerNotes.ROOT: Root is a verb meaning cheer in this baseball song. It is different from the below-ground part of a plant.
answerNotes.HOME: Home can mean a dwelling or the local side in a sporting match. Read the clue before applying the familiar household meaning.
answerNotes.TEAM: A team is a group playing together. In a home-and-away matchup, the home side plays at its own usual venue.
answerNotes.STRIKE: In baseball, a strike can result from a swing and miss. Three strikes normally put the batter out, though foul-ball rules add detail.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.

answerNotes.DAISY: A daisy is a flower with a familiar bright center and raylike outer parts. Daisy is also the name in the bicycle song Daisy Bell.
answerNotes.BICYCLE: A bicycle has two wheels and is driven by pedals. A tandem is a bicycle designed for riders seated one behind another.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.BELL: A bell rings when a clapper or striker vibrates it. A school bell and a decorative handbell use that same basic sound-making idea.
answerNotes.CHAIN: A chain is made from connected links. On a porch swing it provides support; on a bicycle it transfers motion.
answerNotes.FLOWER: A flower is the blossom, rather than the whole plant. In everyday speech, the word can also describe a plant grown for its blooms.
answerNotes.SONG: A song has words and a melody. In the familiar-title puzzles, ordinary definitions help even when a reader does not remember the recording.
answerNotes.ROAD: A road is a route for vehicles. A sidewalk or footpath provides a different part of the journey for people on foot.
